Synthesis and Networks

Synthesis and Networks#

Algorithm synthesis aims to design a convergent optimization algorithm obeying the desired properties.

Networked Algorithms#

Synthesis is posed in terms of a Network separating the oracle \(F\) to the controller (you). These networks can model time-delays, cross-talk, channel memory, and other phenomena.

The default case of no network dynamics (direct connection to the oracle \(F\)) is

\[\begin{split}\mat{c}{ z_k \\ y_k } &= \mat{cc}{0 & I \\ I & 0} \mat{c}{ w_k \\ u_k }.\end{split}\]

The general network \(P\) and controller \(K\) have the descrptions

\[\begin{split}\begin{align} P: & & \mat{c}{ x^N_{k+1} \hl z_k \\ y_k } &= \mat{c|cc}{ A & B_w & B_u \hl C_z & D_{zw} & D_{zu} \\ C_y & D_{yw} & D_{yu} }\mat{c}{ x^N_k \hl w_k \\ u_k } \\ \\ K : & & \mat{c}{ x^c_{k+1} \hl u_k}&=\mat{c|c}{\Ac & \Bc \hl \Cc & \Dc}\mat{c}{ x^c_k \hl y_k }. \end{align}\end{split}\]

The interconnection of \((P, K)\) is well-posed if \(I - D_{zw} \Dc\) is invertible.

Convergence Conditions#

A subsidiary goal in algorithm synthesis is to ensure that the interconnection \((F, (P, K))\) satisfies the convergence conditions for optimization algorithms.

The Regulator Equation condition in the networked setting can be expanded into

  1. Regulator Equation: There is a unique solution \((\Pi, \Gamma, \Phi, \Theta)\) to the linear system of equations

\[\begin{split}\begin{align} \mat{c|cc:c}{A & 0 & B_w N & B_y \hl C_z & \1 & D_{zw}N & D_{zy} \hdl C_y & 0 & D_{yz}N & D_{yu}} \mat{c}{\Pi\hl I\hdl \Gamma}&=\mat{c}{\Pi \hl 0 \hdl \Phi}, \label{eq:nominal_regulation_control_sys_plant} \\ \mat{c|c}{\Ac&\Bc\hl \Cc&\Dc} \mat{c}{\Theta\\\Phi} &= \mat{c}{\Theta \\ \Gamma}. \label{eq:nominal_regulation_control_sys_control} \end{align}\end{split}\]

If there does not exist a \((\Pi, \Gamma, \Phi)\) triple satisfying the top equation, then a convergent optimization algorithm cannot be found.

Under the Convergence and Regulator Equation conditions, convergence in all signals is achieved as

\[\begin{split}\begin{align} \lim_{k \rightarrow \infty} \mat{c}{x_k^N \\ x^c_k \hl y_k \\u_k} & = \mat{c}{\Pi \\ \Theta \hl \Phi \\ \Gamma} \mat{c}{-\beta^* \\ \hat{w}^*}, & \lim_{k \rightarrow \infty} \mat{c}{z_k \\ w_k } & = \mat{c}{z^* \\ w^*} = \mat{c}{\1 \otimes \beta^* \\ N \hat{w}^*}. \end{align}\end{split}\]

The fixed-point matrix for the closed-loop system is

\[\begin{split}\begin{align} \mathbf{X}^* & := \mat{c}{\Pi \\ \Theta}, & \lim_{k \rightarrow \infty} x_k & := \mathbf{X}^* \mat{c}{-\beta^* \\ \hat{w}^*} \end{align}\end{split}\]

Synthesis#

The Regulator Equation requirement enforces structure on possible controllers. We choose controllers \(\Kc\) as the interconnection of an internal model [1] and a subcontroller \(K_f\). This interconnection with \(K = (\text{Model}, K_f)\) involves

\[\begin{split}\begin{align*} \text{Model}: \mat{c}{ v_{k+1} \hl \tilde{y}_k } &= \mat{c|c:cc}{ I & 0 & I & 0 \hl -\Gamma & 0 & 0 & I \\ \Phi & I & 0 & 0 }\mat{c}{ v_k \hl y_k \hdl \tilde{u}_k^1 \\ \tilde{u}_k^2 }, \\ K_f: \mat{c}{ x^c^f_{k+1} \hl \tilde{u}^1_k \\ \tilde{u}^1_k} &=\mat{c|c}{A_f & B_f \hl C_{f1} & D_{f1} \\ C_{f2} & D_{f2}}\mat{c}{ x^c^f_k \hl \tilde{y}_k }. \end{align*}\end{split}\]

Any subcontroller \(K_f\) will ensure that the Regulator Equation requirement in \(K\) is satisfied. The subcontroller \(K_f\) must then ensure that the interconnection \((F, (P, \text{Model}, K_f))\) is well-posed and obeys the convergence and performance requirements. Solving for \(K_f\) can be accomplished through IQC synthesis methods [2].

Synthesis may also involve selecting a solution \((\Pi, \Gamma, \Phi)\) to the regulator equations [3].

[1]

Bruce A Francis and Walter Murray Wonham. The internal model principle of control theory. Automatica, 12(5):457–465, 1976.

[2]

Joost Veenman and Carsten W Scherer. IQC-synthesis with general dynamic multipliers. IFAC Proceedings Volumes, 44(1):4600–4605, 2011.

[3]

C. Scherer, P. Gahinet, and M. Chilali. Multiobjective Output-Feedback Control via LMI Optimization . IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control, 42(7):896–911, 1997. doi:10.1109/9.599969.
